ia_hoot_bluff.blurb: A compact limestone bluff in Jackson County, a short drive from Canton, with about twenty climbs. Nearly everything is bolted sport, with a single trad line and one boulder problem. The wall leans past vertical and the style is steady, juggy pulling rather than delicate face work. Difficulty starts around 5.7, but the real weight sits between 5.10 and 5.12, with a lone 5.13 at the top, so it suits intermediate to strong climbers more than first-timers. Facing south, it catches the sun, which makes it an attractive pick when cold weather shuts down other Iowa crags. The cliff top sits above open farmland, so the wall is easy to miss from the road.

ky_4_fiscal_cliff.blurb: The tallest wall in the Cliffview preserve of the Red River Gorge, rising past 110 feet, and one wall within the larger Fed zone. It holds roughly thirty climbs, almost all bolted sport lines plus a handful of trad. Grades begin near 5.7, with a few 5.9s, then pile up through 5.10, 5.11 and 5.12, finishing with a few 5.13 lines, so strong intermediates will find the most to do. Its reputation rests on good 5.11 and 5.12 pitches. Many lines are long enough that a 70 m rope is recommended, and you should knot the end. The wall faces mostly east, with sun arriving in the late morning.

ky_murder_branch.blurb: A small cluster of sandstone walls on forest road land near Cave Run Lake, outside Morehead, with close to thirty routes split between sport and trad. It breaks into three separate walls strung along one road. The first is a sunny wall next to the road with easy top access, handy for beginners and for learning to rappel. The next has a handful of sport lines and a couple of good trad climbs, plus slabs under a big roof that stay dry in the rain. The farthest wall, deeper in the woods, holds the best-known lines. Most routes fall between 5.8 and 5.10, with a few easier and a few 5.11s. Crowds are rare.

ky_chaos.blurb: A sandstone crag in the Miller Fork preserve of the Red River Gorge, with about 27 climbs: mostly bolted sport, a few trad lines. The wall is split in character. The left half sits in an amphitheater and picks up morning light, though its base can be damp and buggy in summer. The right half looks north and stays shaded for most of the day. Grades run from easy 5.5 up to a 5.14, but the bulk lies in 5.11 and 5.12, so this is mainly a destination for strong sport climbers. Expect some slabby lines and an overhanging section. The walk-in climbs a steep side trail to the base.

ky_hazel_hollow.blurb: A small, easily reached crag in the Bald Rock preserve of the Red River Gorge. It has 26 climbs, about 22 of them sport and the rest moderate trad. The grade range is wide for such a small spot, from a 5.5 up to 5.12, and the heart of it is 5.9 to 5.11, which makes it a good place to collect quality moderates, both on tall and short lines. Sun and shade are mixed through the day. Trails and staging areas were built before the routes went in, so the base is tidy. Reaching the wall involves a short hill with a wooden ladder, and most lines start from the staging area just above it.
